questions.question_text: Read the provided unseen passage tracking the evolution of artificial intelligence in modern education. Based on the passage, what is the primary concern raised by educators regarding AI-generated student assignments?
options: A) The assignments are too complex for teachers to evaluate
B) A severe decline in original critical thinking and authentic academic effort
C) AI systems cost too much money for public schools
D) AI generates too many grammatical errors
questions.answer: B) A severe decline in original critical thinking and authentic academic effort

questions.question_text: According to the passage, which positive outcome do AI tutors provide that traditional classrooms struggle to offer?
options: B) Personalized learning paces adapted to individual student weaknesses in real-time
C) Automated grading of physical sports activities
D) Free internet access for all students
questions.answer: B) Personalized learning paces adapted to individual student weaknesses in real-time

questions.question_text: Complete the sentence based on the passage: To maintain academic integrity, schools are increasingly relying on ________ to detect AI-written essays.
questions.answer: C) specialized digital plagiarism scanners

questions.question_text: How does the author of the passage suggest teachers should shift their testing methods in the AI era? [30-40 words]
questions.answer: The author suggests that teachers should move away from traditional take-home essays and focus on in-class oral presentations, unassisted written exams, and collaborative project-based assessments where students must demonstrate real-time understanding.

questions.question_text: Based on the text, explain why the author believes completely banning AI in schools is a 'shortsighted' strategy. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: The author argues banning AI is shortsighted because these tools will dominate future workplaces. Instead of banning them, schools must teach students how to use AI ethically and effectively as assistants, not replacements for thought.

questions.question_text: Identify the word from paragraph 3 which means 'to integrate or combine smoothly into a larger system'. [1-2 words]
questions.answer: Assimilate

sections.section_name: Section B - Writing Skills & Applied Grammar

questions.question_text: Identify the option that correctly converts the given direct dialog into Reported Speech: The teacher said to the students, "Have you completed the science project?"
options: A) The teacher asked the students if they had completed the science project.
B) The teacher told the students to complete the science project.
C) The teacher asked the students that have they completed the science project.
D) The teacher questions the students if they complete the science project.
questions.answer: A) The teacher asked the students if they had completed the science project.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank with the correct tense form: By the time the fire brigade arrived, the building ________ (engulf) in flames.
questions.answer: C) had been engulfed

questions.question_text: Choose the correct modal to fill in the blank: You ________ wear a helmet while riding a motorcycle; it is the law.
questions.answer: D) must

questions.question_text: Identify the error in Subject-Verb Concord in this sentence and select the correct replacement: 'Neither the principal nor the teachers is attending the seminar today.'
questions.answer: A) Change 'is' to 'are'

questions.question_text: Choose the correct determiner to complete the sentence: ________ students in the class were able to solve that difficult math equation.
questions.answer: C) Few

questions.question_text: Convert this command into Reported Speech: The manager said to the clerk, "Do not leave the office until the files are updated."
options: A) The manager asked the clerk to not leave the office until the files are updated.
B) The manager ordered the clerk not to leave the office until the files were updated.
C) The manager said to the clerk do not leave the office until the files were updated.
D) The manager warned the clerk that he should not leave the office.
questions.answer: B) The manager ordered the clerk not to leave the office until the files were updated.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank with the correct tense: I ________ (wait) for the bus for over an hour before I finally decided to walk home.
questions.answer: C) had been waiting

questions.question_text: Select the correct modal for polite request: ________ I borrow your laptop for a quick presentation?
questions.answer: B) Could

questions.question_text: Write a formal letter of inquiry to the Director of a reputed coaching institute, asking for details regarding their upcoming crash course for engineering entrance exams. Mention your specific requirements. [100-120 words]
questions.answer: Sir/Madam, I am writing to inquire about the engineering entrance crash course advertised in Sunday's newspaper. I am currently in Class 12 and wish to enroll in an intensive preparatory program. Kindly provide detailed information regarding the duration of the course, batch timings, and the total fee structure, including study material costs. Additionally, please clarify if you offer weekend-only batches, as my regular school hours extend till 3 PM on weekdays. I would also appreciate details regarding your faculty profile and past success rates. I look forward to receiving this information promptly so I can initiate the admission process. Yours faithfully, Rohit/Riya.

questions.question_text: Write an analytical paragraph based on a given pie chart showing the shifting dietary habits of teenagers (40% Fast Food, 30% Processed Snacks, 20% Home Cooked, 10% Fruits/Veggies) over the last decade. [100-120 words]
questions.answer: The provided pie chart illustrates a concerning trend in the dietary habits of teenagers over the past decade. A staggering 70% of their daily diet consists of unhealthy options, divided between fast food (40%) and processed snacks (30%). This dominance of calorie-dense, low-nutrition food highlights a shift toward convenience over health. Conversely, traditional home-cooked meals account for only 20% of their intake. Most alarmingly, fresh fruits and vegetables make up a mere 10% of their diet, indicating a severe deficiency in essential vitamins and minerals. This data underscores an urgent need for nutritional education and parental intervention to prevent long-term health crises like obesity among the youth.

questions.question_text: Read the extract from 'A Letter to God'. Why did Lencho become angry when he finally counted the money inside the envelope?
options: A) Because the postmaster had signed it
B) Because the money was counterfeit
C) Because there were only seventy pesos instead of the hundred he requested
D) Because the letter contained no message from God
questions.answer: C) Because there were only seventy pesos instead of the hundred he requested

questions.question_text: Read the extract from 'The Thief's Story'. What was Hari Singh's primary realization that made him return to Anil with the stolen money?
options: A) He realized the police were already looking for him
B) He realized that without Anil's education, he would remain a petty thief forever
C) He realized the money was not enough to escape
D) He felt guilty about breaking the locks
questions.answer: B) He realized that without Anil's education, he would remain a petty thief forever

questions.question_text: In the poem 'Dust of Snow', how does the poet Robert Frost describe the sudden change in his mood? [30-40 words]
questions.answer: The poet was initially in a state of deep sorrow and regret. However, when a crow shook a hemlock tree, causing fine dust of snow to fall on him, his gloomy mood instantly shifted to one of joy, saving the rest of his day.

questions.question_text: According to Nelson Mandela in 'Long Walk to Freedom', what are the 'twin obligations' every man has in life? [30-40 words]
questions.answer: Mandela states every man has twin obligations: the first is a personal obligation to his family, parents, wife, and children. The second is a broader social obligation to his people, his community, and his country.

questions.question_text: Why was the young seagull afraid to fly in 'His First Flight', and how did his mother finally compel him to do so? [40-50 words]
questions.answer: The young seagull was paralyzed by the fear that his wings would not support him over the vast sea. His mother compelled him by flying close to him with a piece of fish but halting just out of reach. Maddened by hunger, he dove at the food, falling outward and instinctively spreading his wings to fly.

questions.question_text: In 'A Triumph of Surgery', how did Mr. Herriot effectively cure Tricki without using any medical treatments or surgery? [40-50 words]
questions.answer: Dr. Herriot cured Tricki by strictly controlling his diet and increasing his physical activity. He cut off all the rich, sugary foods Mrs. Pumphrey provided and only gave him plenty of water initially. Tricki was forced to run and play with other dogs, naturally shedding his excess fat and regaining his energy.

questions.question_text: Analyze the character of Anne Frank based on her diary entries. How did writing in a diary help her cope with her isolation and the challenges of adolescence? [80-100 words]
questions.answer: Anne Frank emerges as a highly intelligent, perceptive, and deeply lonely teenager. Despite having family and friends, she felt a profound lack of a true confidante with whom she could share her deepest vulnerabilities. The diary, which she named 'Kitty', became her non-judgmental best friend. Writing provided her with a psychological anchor, allowing her to process her complex emotions regarding her mother's criticism, the oppressive isolation of the Secret Annex, and the terror of the Holocaust. Through her articulate entries, Anne transformed her fear and adolescent confusion into profound introspection, proving her emotional maturity and offering her a necessary escape from her grim reality.

questions.question_text: Griffin was a brilliant scientist but a lawless person. Evaluate this statement with reference to his actions in 'Footprints Without Feet'. Do you think his discovery brought him any real benefit? [80-100 words]
questions.answer: Griffin was undoubtedly a brilliant scientist who achieved the impossible by discovering a drug that made the human body invisible. However, his brilliance was overshadowed by his lack of morality and empathy. He misused his discovery entirely for selfish and destructive purposes: setting fire to his landlord's house for revenge, stealing clothes from a London store, and robbing a theatrical company and a clergyman. Ultimately, his discovery brought him no real benefit. Instead of fame or wealth, invisibility brought him isolation, constant fear, and the physical misery of being naked in the freezing London winter. His lawlessness turned a scientific triumph into a personal curse.
